metadata.title: Evaluating Contextual Input and Shared Representation in Multi-Metric Runtime Forecasting for Cloud Software Systems: Minimal Revision Protocol v0.4
metadata.description:
This is a prospective registration of the v0.4 minimal revision protocol, using secondary data.

The Bitbrains GWA-T-12 datasets already existed, and this project's historical v1 results and post-hoc controls on them were observed before this registration. This is not a retrospective preregistration of v1.

v0.4 supersedes the v0.3 strengthening protocol (OSF registration kuwra) before any v0.3 execution: no v0.3 scientific fit, outer-test evaluation or analysis ever occurred. kuwra is not withdrawn. This registration prospectively governs only the new v0.4 runs. No v0.4 scientific fit, outer-test evaluation or analysis occurred before registration. Development testing used only synthetic or tiny generated models and data, and no v0.4 runtime journal exists.

All v0.4 analyses are descriptive (tier 2 extension): no confirmatory hypothesis tests, p-values or multiplicity corrections.

The frozen protocol (analysis_plan_v0.4.md, SHA-256 76652ad9231eed63245f38d2c7a80a73752a9f3b9fefdb0bd31e3c225af4b80f) and the execution and analysis code are fixed by Git tag fgcs-v04-registration-package (commit 9b94a066d2818ac726205954cb53f52e0ec3371d), package digest 242772484617d4c21b6694b124540eebab60588d5e856b4b4a613498aa2e8442 and execution seal babe1fefa7f48c462b7f628d3d98507ec03779a31df843cb7d6f044d257abd15.

An independent audit of this package passed with non-blocking notes. The sealed inputs not held in Git are archived at Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.24189108 (reused from v0.3 unchanged). Their manifest has SHA-256 cb2b005c5927729e76724072046f4e32f12478fccceaa3b22d5f9e179e720a3e.

registration_responses.72-2:
This prospective revision study asks, for multi-resource runtime forecasting of cloud telemetry (CPU, THROUGHPUT, MEMORY, DISK_WRITE) on 20 Bitbrains VMs:
(1) How do modern baselines (DLinear, PatchTST-style and iTransformer-style) compare with the LSTM, cell by cell?
(2) Are contextual input (own resource versus all four resources) and representation sharing (independent per-target models versus one shared model) separable design decisions? Each backbone is studied as a 2x2 of S1, S2, M0 and M1, with the contrasts S2:S1 and M1:M0 (context) and M0:S1 and M1:S2 (sharing).
(3) Is shared-representation degradation associated with cross-resource dependence, task affinity, gradient conflict or loss imbalance (diagnostics D-1 to D-7)?
All three questions are answered descriptively (protocol v0.4, P0-P5).
registration_responses.72-4:
There are no confirmatory hypotheses. All v0.4 analyses are descriptive: no p-values, hypothesis tests or multiplicity families (protocol P0).

Endpoint: native MAE, averaged over seeds 0-2 within each block x entity x fold x resource x horizon x cell. MacroMAE gives those cells equal weight, then every horizon equal weight. The primary summary is the MacroMAE gain G(C:B) = 100 (MacroMAE(B) - MacroMAE(C)) / MacroMAE(B) per contrast, resource, block and backbone.

Each gain gets the paper's consistency class (Broad Positive, Conditionally Positive, Broad Negative, Neutral or Mixed), with seed thresholds unchanged and VM thresholds rescaled to 10 VMs per block: horizons 4/5, 3/5, 1/5; VMs 8/10, 5/10, 2/10; folds 4/5, 3/5, 1/5; seeds 2/3, 2/3, 1/3. An effect generalises across backbones only if every backbone for which the contrast is defined has a non-neutral class of the same sign; otherwise it is backbone-dependent.

Gradient conflict is not assumed to explain sharing degradation. Null, mixed or conflicting results are valid outcomes and will be reported as such.
registration_responses.72-7:
- Bitbrains GWA-T-12 fastStorage: VMs 697, 860, 366, 679, 360, 505, 481, 109, 680, 50.
- Bitbrains GWA-T-12 Rnd: VMs 99, 409, 269, 493, 474, 97, 118, 233, 142, 151.

These are the first 10 VMs per block by frozen v1 cohort rank, already frozen in v0.3; they were selected by rank, not by any outcome. Resources: CPU, THROUGHPUT, MEMORY, DISK_WRITE. Five purged expanding outer folds, each with one inner train/validation split; horizons 1, 2, 4, 9 and 18 steps; every model uses the frozen v1 H64-M1-selected context for each entity and fold. registration_responses.72-24:
Resources: CPU, THROUGHPUT, MEMORY, DISK_WRITE, per VM time series. Measured: native MAE per backbone, cell, block, VM, resource, fold, horizon and seed; persistence skill against reused v1 persistence.

Diagnostics (P5): D-1 lagged cross-correlation between resources (lags 1-18, inner-training windows only); D-2 reused Ridge ARX:AR gain; D-3 Spearman association of D-1 or D-2 with the LSTM context and sharing effects; D-4 LSTM gradient cosines, norm ratio and excess conflict K at the final selected epoch; D-5/D-6 pairwise and leave-one-out task affinity from an all-input LSTM transfer lattice; D-7 per-task training-loss shares. Blocks, cohort, horizons and contexts are defined in the registered configuration protocol_v04.json, referenced by hash in PACKAGE.json.
registration_responses.72-29: Backbone (LSTM, DLinear, PatchTST-style, iTransformer-style); cell (input scope own or all x independent or shared parameters: S1, S2, M0, M1; iTransformer S1/M0 are structurally undefined and not fitted); and, for D-5, the retained task subset (6 pairs, 4 leave-one-out triples).
registration_responses.72-33:
Native MAE per backbone, cell, block, VM, resource, fold, horizon and seed.
Diagnostics: D-1 maximum absolute lagged correlation; D-2 G(ARX:AR); D-4 cosines, norm ratio and K; D-6 F and Q affinity log ratios; D-7 loss shares.
registration_responses.72-35:
No exclusions or replacements.
- A fit that still fails after its retries makes that block x VM x fold x resource x seed missing for every cell of that backbone's 2x2, so contrasts stay paired; seed averages use the remaining seeds, consistency predicates use fractions of the units still available, and every missing unit is listed.
- Same-seal retries are allowed only for interruptions and infrastructure errors, at most two per identity; code repairs require a chained seal amendment (v0.3 C3).
- Outer-test data are read only after fit closure, and the analysis only after evaluation closure (v0.3 C6). Closure is final.
registration_responses.72-37: The VM. Cell MAEs are seed-averaged and aggregated within VM; the paired VM-cluster bootstrap resamples VMs within each block (protocol P4).
registration_responses.72-39: No outlier exclusion: every registered cell is retained, with no exclusions or replacements.
registration_responses.72-41: None. Seeds, then entity-fold cells, then horizons receive equal weights (MacroMAE); blocks are reported separately and never pooled; no pooled cross-backbone statistic is computed (protocol P4).
registration_responses.72-44: This project's v1 study (the tier-1 frozen primary study: S1, S2 and M1 LSTM forecasters, three seeds, on TimeTrack, Bitbrains and Materna) and its post-hoc controls (common-context S2, M1-H129, Ridge AR/ARX, persistence) are reported in a manuscript under journal review, with known results. TimeTrack is also described in Meliani et al., ICC 2025.
registration_responses.72-46:
The authors have previously accessed, analysed and observed these datasets and the v1 results, including the v1-selected contexts, cohorts and per-model errors, and the post-hoc controls including Ridge AR/ARX. D-2 reuses those already-observed Ridge results and is labelled post hoc.

The v0.4 design fixes from v1 metadata: contexts (frozen v1 H64-M1-selected L); the 20-VM cohort (first 10 per block by frozen rank); folds and origins. Compute was estimated from component timings and a synthetic worker benchmark (random tensors), not from any v0.4 outcome.

v0.3 (OSF kuwra) was superseded before any v0.3 execution. No v0.4 scientific fit, outer-test evaluation or analysis occurred before registration.
registration_responses.72-49: Paired VM-cluster bootstrap within each block: 10 VMs resampled with replacement, all five folds and the paired cell structure kept, on seed-averaged matched MAEs; 10,000 replicates, percentile 95% intervals, PCG64 seed 20261007, one draw matrix per block (fastStorage then Rnd) reused for every interval in that block. D-3 uses Spearman correlation with average ranks and the same draws. Intervals never enter the consistency classes. No hypothesis tests.
registration_responses.72-51: MacroMAE gain G (percent), entity log effect D(C:B) = ln A_C - ln A_B, the interaction log-ratio I = ln A_M1 - ln A_S2 - ln A_M0 + ln A_S1, matched-cell median MAE ratio and win rate, persistence skill, and Spearman rho for D-3.
registration_responses.72-53: The design is fixed (20 VMs, 5 folds, 3 seeds), with no power target or minimum effect size. Intervals at 10 VMs per block are expected to be wide (protocol P11).
registration_responses.72-55: No inferential criteria: no p-values or significance thresholds. Effects are summarised by the consistency classes and the cross-backbone rule above; bootstrap intervals are reported separately and never enter the classes. Associations (D-3) are descriptive, not causal.
registration_responses.72-57:
Rules fixed in the protocol and the sealed analysis code:
- Missing fits: the P4 missing-fit rule above. Failures in the D-5 transfer lattice do not mask the 2x2 results; each D-6 entry drops only units missing in its own two cells.
- Undefined values: a gain with a zero or missing reference, or a predicate with no available units, gives the class "Undefined", which counts as backbone-dependent in the cross-backbone summary. Persistence skill is undefined when a horizon has no usable cell; zero-denominator skills are counted, not replaced.
- Bootstrap: replicates whose statistic is undefined are dropped from the percentile and counted.
- Interaction: the reported I is the mean over VMs of the entity I, with its VM-cluster interval.
- D-3: needs at least 3 VMs with both values, in the point estimate and in each replicate; VMs lacking a value drop out of both.
- D-1: series value at each inner-training origin; lag pairs only within contiguous segments; entity value per target is the mean over folds of the mean over the three source resources of the maximum absolute correlation.
- D-4: cosines averaged over the 8 batch pairs, the norm ratio over both batches of each pair, then over folds x seeds per VM; a slot with undefined K is dropped.
- D-7: block-level mean shares per epoch, over the fits reaching that epoch.
- Baseline-accuracy table: backbones compared on their common available units.
registration_responses.72-59:
The scientific runtime and the analysis are fixed by execution seal babe1fefa7f48c462b7f628d3d98507ec03779a31df843cb7d6f044d257abd15, checked by an independent audit. Every new model cell passes structural checks before any data fit. Exactly six single-threaded CPU workers; a 90-fit canary is reviewed (technical evidence only) before the remaining fits.

Robustness and context are descriptive: matched persistence skill, the baseline-accuracy table, parameter counts, and the reused tier-1 results and post-hoc controls (reported separately). Declared compromises (P11): a reduced 20-VM cohort, no Materna or TimeTrack reruns, three seeds, fixed untuned hyperparameters, LSTM-selected contexts imposed on every backbone, design-defined cells (iTransformer S1/M0 undefined; DLinear M1 shares only through a rank-16 bottleneck), LSTM-only gradient diagnostics, affinity from empirical transfer, partly reused dependence evidence, and no interventions.
registration_responses.72-61: Everything in v0.4 is exploratory and descriptive (tier 2): the 2x2 contrasts, the baseline comparison and all mechanism diagnostics D-1 to D-7. Tier-1 and tier-2 results are always reported separately. No intervention (Huber, PCGrad, GradNorm, task grouping) is part of v0.4; any such run needs a separate, later registration.
